# Udayamāṇavapucchā (Snp 5.14 (PTS Snp 214))
**ID:** Snp 5.14 (PTS Snp 214)
**Section:** Suttanipāta (snp)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Udayamāṇavapucchā* ("The Questions of the Student Udaya", Snp 5.14, PTS Snp 214, verses 1105–1111) is a verse discourse belonging to the *Pārāyanavagga* of the *Suttanipāta*, recognized as representing some of the oldest material in the Pali Canon [SuttaCentral; Barua 1921; Norman 1997-2001]. Set as an inquiry by the young brahmin Udaya, the text addresses the attainment of unbinding and the cessation of consciousness [SuttaCentral; Barua 1921]. Metrically composed in Śloka, the poem holds an important place in early Buddhist meditative practice [Wynne 2007]. Its middle verses appear to characterize the stillness of the mind (*āneñja*) associated with the fourth *jhāna*, though divergent from standard doctrinal formulas [Pande 1974], while its concluding verses highlight the cultivation of mindfulness regarding internal and external sensations (*ajjhattaṁ* and *bahiddhā*) to abandon craving and liberate the mind [Wynne 2007].
Canonical exegesis is preserved in the *Cullaniddesa* (*Udayamāṇavapucchāniddesa*, Cnd 17; also Cnd 2), which DharmaNexus identifies as sharing extensive passages of text reuse [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. Verses are also shared within the Pali canon with the *Devatā Saṁyutta* (SN 1) and the *Tikanipāta* (AN 3.33), the latter corroborated as a parallel by SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. Further cross-tradition parallels to individual verses occur across various recensions of the Dharmapada/Udānavarga literature, including the Pali Dhammapada (Dhp 386), the Gāndhārī Dharmapada, the Patna Dharmapada, the Chinese *Faju jing* (T 210.35), the Sanskrit Udānavarga (UV 33), and the *Śarīrārthagāthā* in the *Yogācārabhūmi*, where verses parallel to Sn 1110–1111 appear in the *Ajitapraśna* section [SuttaCentral; Lee 2017]. DharmaNexus additionally identifies automated cross-language alignments with the Tibetan *Devatā-sūtra* (D0329) and the Chinese *Saṁyuktāgama* (T 99) [DharmaNexus].
